sections.toxoplasmosis_in_cats_and_humans_symptom:
Abstract 
 Cats are elegant, affectionate, and intuitive creatures that have shared a deep bond with humans for centuries. Their calming presence, playful energy, and unique personalities make them treasured members of countless homes. Beyond companionship, cats influence human emotional well-being, offering comfort, reducing stress, and enriching daily life with their gentle behaviors. However, as close as this relationship is, living with cats also means understanding certain health considerations. Let’s dive into this topic and discover how ancient wisdom can guide safe and harmonious living with our beloved cats.
sections.introduction: Toxoplasmosis is a significant cat-associated zoonotic infection caused by the protozoan parasite Toxoplasma gondii. It naturally infects cats, which serve as its definitive hosts, and can spread to humans and other animals through contaminated food, water, or soil. While most infections remain asymptomatic, toxoplasmosis can pose serious risks for pregnant women and immunocompromised individuals. Understanding its transmission, symptoms, and preventive measures is essential for safeguarding both human and animal health.

sections.diagnosis_of_toxoplasmosis_in_cats:
To check if a cat has toxoplasmosis, vets mainly rely on tests because most cats don’t show clear symptoms. 
 1. Blood Tests 

 IgM shows a recent infection 
 IgG shows an old infection 

 2. PCR Test 
 Checks for the parasite’s DNA — very accurate. 
 3. Stool Test 
 Looks for parasite eggs in poop, but cats shed them only for a short time. 
 4. Physical Check-Up 
 Vet checks for fever, weakness, breathing issues, or eye problems. 
 5. Scans (If Needed) 
 X-ray or ultrasound to see if organs are affected. 
 Understanding Cat-To-Human Transmission Of Toxoplasmosis 
 Toxoplasmosis spreads from cats to humans mainly through indirect exposure, meaning the parasite usually reaches humans through contaminated surroundings rather than direct contact with the cat itself. Cats play a key role because they are the only hosts in which the parasite Toxoplasma gondii can complete its life cycle. 
 How Cats Become Infected 
 Cats acquire the parasite when they: 

 Hunt and eat infected rodents or birds 
 Consume raw or undercooked meat containing the parasite 
 Once infected, a cat may shed millions of microscopic oocysts (eggs) in its feces—but usually only for 1–3 weeks in its lifetime 

 How These Oocysts Become Infectious 
 Freshly passed oocysts are not infectious immediately. They need 1 to 5 days in soil, litter, or environment to become infectious. Once matured, they can survive in: 

 Soil 
 Sand 
 Grass 
 Carpets 
 Litter boxes 
 Garden areas 

 They are extremely resistant and may remain infectious for months. 
 How Humans Get Infected 

 Cleaning a litter box containing infected feces and touching mouth, face, food, or kitchen items without washing hands. 
 Oocysts can stick to hands while gardening, touching soil, sand, mud, or plants grown in contaminated soil. 
 Eating unwashed vegetables, fruits, or herbs grown in contaminated soil. 
 Oocysts may spread through shoes, cat paws, floors, carpets, and dust. 
 Contaminated water can also carry infectious oocysts.
sections.which_people_are_at_higher_risk:
Certain people are more likely to get sick from toxoplasmosis. These include: 

 Pregnant women 
 People with weak immunity (HIV/AIDS, chemotherapy) 
 Organ transplant patients 
 Infants or very young children 
 Elderly individuals
sections.symptoms_of_toxoplasmosis_in_humans:
Many people infected with toxoplasmosis do not show any symptoms. But when symptoms do appear, they are usually mild and similar to common infections. 
 1. Common Symptoms 

 Mild fever 
 Headache 
 Tiredness or weakness 
 Body aches or muscle pain 
 Swollen lymph nodes (usually in the neck) 

 2. Less Common Symptoms 

 Blurred vision or eye pain 
 Confusion or trouble concentrating (rare) 

 Precautions By Humans 
 Simple preventive steps can significantly reduce the chances of infection: 

 Wash hands thoroughly after handling raw meat. 
 Cook all meats well until no pink juices remain; avoid rare or medium-rare dishes. 
 Wash vegetables properly to remove any soil. 
 Clean hands carefully before eating. 
 Immediately wash knives, cutting boards, and utensils used for raw meat. 
 Wear gloves while gardening. 
 Avoid direct contact with cats. 
 Ask someone else to clean litter trays. 
 Ensure litter trays are cleaned and disinfected daily using proper hygiene, as cat faeces need at least 24 hours for oocysts to become infective.
sections.diagnosis_of_toxoplasmosis_in_humans:
Diagnosing toxoplasmosis is mainly done through blood tests and, when needed, a few additional examinations. 
 1. Blood Tests (Main Method) 
 For checking antibodies made by the body: 

 IgM antibodies 
 IgG antibodies 

 2. PCR Test 
 A highly accurate test that detects the parasite’s DNA in blood or body fluids. 
 3. Eye Examination 
 If the infection affects the eyes, an eye specialist checks for inflammation or retinal damage. 
 4. Imaging Tests (Only If Necessary) 
 Ultrasound, CT scan, or MRI may be used in special cases—especially if organs or the nervous system may be affected.

sections.symptoms_based_on_tridosha_and_dhatu_inv:
Pitta increases → fever, inflammation, eye involvement 
 Kapha increases → lymph node swelling, heaviness, fatigue 
 Vata may get affected → in severe cases (neurological issues) 

 Thus, the infection moves from external cause → internal dosha imbalance. 
 As the parasite spreads, it affects deeper tissues: 

 Rasa Dhatu: Lymphatic system 
 Rakta Dhatu → Blood 
 Mamsa Dhatu: muscles, body aches 
 Majja Dhatu → brain and nerves (in severe cases) 

 As read earlier, Humans also get infected from Toxoplasmosis via Cats, but for them also the pathophysiology remains same and it comes under Agantuj Vyadhi only. Firstly tridosha gets vitiated and then dhatus gets affected afterwards and leads to various symptoms already discussed above.
